name: Amiri
genre: Naskh text type: revival of the 1905 Bulaq/Amiriya type
source: Khaled Hosny, Sebastian Kosch / Google Fonts
notes: The anchor: the clean side of the AL08/AL09 medium pair. Broad-nib width logic intact; many ligatures and stacked forms

name: Amiri Typewriter
licence: OFL 1.1 (OFL.txt in repo; GitHub's licence field says NOASSERTION)
notes: Modelled on old Arabic typewriters: one shape for isolated/final, one for initial/medial; fixed advance with overhangs. A mechanised office-print hand

name: Rakkas
genre: Ruq'ah lettering on 1950s-60s Egyptian movie posters
notes: The closest font to the Egyptian poster-title look; contextual alternates cascade vertically. The clean partner for AP01

name: Lalezar
notes: Bold, dynamic poster display: Persian, but the same era and medium

name: Jomhuria
notes: Dark stencil display: stencil bridges cut strokes in a regular rhythm. Print-shop vernacular

name: Blaka Hollow (+ Blaka solid / Blaka Ink)
genre: blackletter x Kufi, reed-pen logic; hollow = outlined cut
notes: The only open Arabic outline-style face found: every stroke is a double contour (parallel contiguous lines). The solid cut gives the fill, so the offset can be measured

name: Reem Kufi
genre: Kufic on the Fatimid grid, after Mohammed Abdul Qadir's 20th-c. formalisation
notes: Geometric, which Ian asked for: straight runs, designed angles, near-monoline, long baseline extensions

name: Reem Kufi Ink / Reem Kufi Fun (colour)
notes: Colour layers behave like chromatic wood type: one layer per pen. Needs a COLR-aware reader

name: Qahiri
genre: manuscript Kufic regularised by Mohammad Abdul Qadir
notes: The most geometric face here, close to a construction grid; the geometry pole against the Naskh scans

name: Kufam
source: Wael Morcos, Artur Schmal / Google Fonts
notes: Dark condensed signage Kufi; contemporary

name: Aref Ruqaa (and Aref Ruqaa Ink)
genre: classical Ruq'a (the everyday and sign-writer's hand)
source: Abdullah Aref, Khaled Hosny / Google Fonts
notes: Calligraphic Ruq'a, the hand behind much shop-sign and poster lettering. With AF03: the hand vs its poster display form

name: Katibeh
genre: Naskh with Thuluth qualities; archaic headline
notes: Nearest open face to hot-metal headline Naskh

name: Mada
genre: modernist unmodulated face from Cairo road signage
notes: Signage vernacular; monoline at light weights

name: Marhey, Lemonada, El Messiri
genre: hand-lettering display; Naskh with Diwani influence; brush-drawn Naskh
notes: Lettering and brush feel but contemporary; low priority

name: Badeen Display
genre: display bridging youth culture and Arab pop heritage
notes: Retro-pop intent; thick/thin with sharp and round edges

name: Noto Kufi Arabic
notes: Geometric control. At wght 100 it is near-monoline, so the skeleton is almost free: use it to check the centreline extractor

name: Noto Naskh Arabic, Scheherazade New
notes: No-period-flavour Naskh controls

name: Alkalami
genre: Kano 'alkalami' (qalam on wooden boards): very thick baseline, hairline verticals
notes: Extreme width profile and stark nib logic; a manuscript tradition, so contrast only. Overlaps the calligraphy agent's scope

name: Handjet
genre: element-based modular (pixel / LED) font with Arabic
notes: Dot-matrix / scoreboard era rather than letterpress; glyphs built from repeated elements

name: Cairo, Tajawal, Almarai, Beiruti, Alexandria, Vazirmatn, Changa, Harmattan
